messages.text: Well I have it here  at my office it's going okay so far i change over to harlo os but am not seeing the hashrate
Read harlolabs.com

I'm H., HeliumDeploy's technical specialist, Sarah passed this over to me.

Good news is that a fresh Harlo OS install usually just needs the pool settings put back, since a factory install wipes them.

One thing first so I point you the right way: in the Harlo OS web UI, does the hashrate field show 0, or is it blank / not loading at all?
it blank and if i restart it will show for a few minutes and go blank again

That pattern (works a few minutes after a restart, then blanks) is useful.

Next check: when the hashrate goes blank, does the rest of the page keep updating, or does everything freeze?

1. Leave the UI open until it blanks.
2. Refresh the page once.
3. Tell me what the temperature, uptime and shares/accepted fields read after that refresh, and whether uptime is still climbing.

If uptime keeps climbing and only hashrate drops out, it is usually the ASIC dropping off or a pool connection issue. If the whole page stops or will not reload, it is the Wi-Fi link.
in the log am still receive files

Good, so the pool is still sending work (those are job notifications) and the network is fine. That points at the ASIC side, not the connection.

One thing to confirm, because it is the usual cause after a Harlo OS install: which device model did you pick in the flasher, and does it match the unit exactly? A mismatched model gives you jobs with no hashrate.

Then paste me the last 5 or 6 log lines from the moment the hashrate goes blank (anything mentioning ASIC, init, or job, and any temperature or voltage line).
i took the thor p2 model

Good, the model matches, so we can rule that out.

Next step is the log. When it goes blank again:

1. Open the log in the Harlo OS UI.
2. Copy me the last 5 or 6 lines from that moment, especially anything with ASIC, init, reset or temp.
3. Tell me the chip temperature and the input voltage shown on the main page.

My suspicion is either the ASIC dropping out of communication, or the board browning out under load (voltage sag from the PSU), and those two look different in the log.
brb
No rush, I'm here. Grab those log lines plus the temperature and voltage when you're back.
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)

That log is actually good news: shares 203 through 212 all accepted, roughly one every couple of seconds, latency around 80 ms. The miner is hashing and the pool is taking the work. So this is a display problem, not a mining problem.

Two quick checks:

1. Hard refresh the UI page (Ctrl+Shift+R, or Cmd+Shift+R on Mac), or open it in a different browser or from your phone. If the number comes back, it was the page caching.
2. Check your pool dashboard for that worker. If the pool shows a sensible hashrate there, the unit is fine and we are only chasing a cosmetic field.

Tell me what the pool side shows and we'll go from there.
Are  you a chat bot?

Yes, I'm an AI assistant. I'm Hal, HeliumDeploy's technical support bot, and I handle the hardware and firmware side of the chat.

If you'd rather have a person on it, say the word and I'll pass you over to the team.

Either way, the finding stands: your log shows shares being accepted steadily, so the Thor P2 is mining. Let me know what your pool dashboard reports for that worker and we can close out the blank hashrate field.
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)

Thanks, same log, and it still reads healthy: ten shares accepted in about 65 seconds.

Doing the math on those share difficulties, your unit is averaging somewhere around 25 TH/s. That is a rough estimate from a short window, so treat it as a ballpark, but it confirms the chip is working. The blank field in the UI is a reporting bug, not lost hashrate.

I've passed this to JD, our hardware lead, with the model, the Harlo OS install and the log, and the team will confirm by email, usually within one business day.

Faster route if you want it solved today: our Discord at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf , mention @nullhashrate (that's JD). He and the community are very active in the Harlo OS channel and he can look at a screenshot of your main UI page right away.

One last thing that often fixes it: in Harlo OS, open Firmware updates and apply the latest OTA image (that keeps your settings, unlike a factory install). If you're a build behind, the blank hashrate field is a known kind of glitch.
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)
Handed to the team · Blank hashrate field persists in Harlo OS UI despite healthy hashing; needs JD t

The team has it now and someone can jump into this chat. If you step away, you'll get the answer by email.

Summary of where we are: the Thor P2 is hashing fine, shares are being accepted, roughly 25 TH/s by the share math. Only the hashrate field in the UI is blank.

Worth trying while you wait:

1. Harlo OS UI, Firmware updates section, apply the latest OTA image (keeps your settings).
2. Hard refresh the page afterwards, or open it from your phone.

And for a same-day answer from JD himself: https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf , mention @nullhashrate.
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)

That pool page looks correct, nothing to change there:

1. Host and port solo.atlaspool.io:3333, Stratum V1, that is the right combination for them.
2. Latency 82 ms and a live difficulty of 4,212 means you are connected and the pool is setting your share target.
3. Allocation 100% to Pool 1, blank password defaults to x, both fine.
4. Your worker is set to your BTC address, which is what solo pools expect.

One thing to know: you are on a solo pool. The miner will show accepted shares all day (your log confirms that), but solo pools often show worker hashrate on their own stats page keyed to your payout address, and some only refresh it every few minutes. So check the atlaspool stats page for your address rather than expecting a dashboard like a shared pool gives.

So: hardware hashing, pool connected, config correct. The only open item is the blank hashrate field in the UI, which JD now has.
why since i change the thor os to harlo os the hashrate does not go above 5 th/s

That changes the picture, thanks. A hard cap ···· spec right after a fresh install is almost always the tuning settings coming back at a conservative default, or not all chips being detected.

From the Harlo OS settings and main page, give me these four numbers:

1. ASIC frequency (MHz)
2. Core voltage (mV)
3. Chip temperature
4. Power draw (watts) and the chip or ASIC count shown

The chip count is the important one: if it reads lower than it should for a Thor P2, the board is only initialising part of the hash chain, and that cap···· fraction of the rated rate no matter what the frequency says.
asic fre 718 C core v 1187 chip temp46.9 power162.5

Those numbers look healthy, and they argue against a real 5 TH/s:

1. 718 MHz and 1187 mV are a normal working pair, not a limp-mode default.
2. 46.9 C is cool, so nothing is thermally throttling.
3. 162.5 W is full-tilt power draw. A board genuinely doing 5 TH/s would not be pulling that. Your log math said roughly 25 TH/s, which fits 162.5 W far better.

So the chips are working and the number on screen is what is wrong, same bug as the blank field.

Two last things for JD:

1. The chip or ASIC count on the main page, the one I asked for. If that reads low, part of the chain is not initialising.
2. Is the 5 TH/s figure the one in the Harlo OS UI, or from the atlaspool stats page?

With the count I can tell you whether this is cosmetic or a real hash chain issue, and JD already has the rest of the case.
